subject.title: California — Proposition 1 (Authorizes Bonds for Housing Affordability Programs)

positions.statement: Transcribed from the voter guide image: "Proposition 1 — NO — California is already deeply in debt."

subject.title: California — Proposition 2 (Increases State's Rainy Day Fund)

positions.statement: Transcribed from the voter guide image: "Proposition 2 — NO — Now is not the time to gut state spending limits, nor to encourage Sacramento politicians to spend even more money they do not have."

subject.title: California — Proposition 3 (Provides Permanent Funding for Schools and Health Care by Extending Existing Tax on High Incomes)

positions.statement: Transcribed from the voter guide image: "Proposition 3 — NO — California taxes are already high enough."

subject.title: California — Proposition 4 (Repeals Prohibition Against Public Funding of Election Campaigns)

positions.statement: Transcribed from the voter guide image: "Proposition 4 — NO — Politicians should not be raiding taxpayer pockets to pay for their election and reelection campaigns."

subject.title: California — Proposition 5 (Changes Recall Election Process for Statewide Officers)

positions.statement: Transcribed from the voter guide image: "Proposition 5 — NO — Voters should be given the choice to recall politicians who aren't doing their jobs."

subject.title: California — Proposition 37 (Creates Loan Program for Middle-Income Buyers of Qualified New Homes)

positions.statement: Transcribed from the voter guide image: "Proposition 37 — NO — California can't even manage its own budget"

subject.title: California — Proposition 38 (Authorizes Bonds for Immunology Medical Research)

positions.statement: Transcribed from the voter guide image: "Proposition 38 — NO — this proposition is just a money-grab by a single California university."

subject.title: California — Proposition 39 (Prohibits Citizens from Voting Unless They Present Government-Issued Identification)

positions.statement: Transcribed from the voter guide image: "Proposition 39 — YES — Voter identification is essential to maintaining the integrity of our elections and preventing wholesale election fraud."

subject.title: California — Proposition 40 (Imposes One-Time Tax on Certain Taxpayers)

positions.statement: Transcribed from the voter guide image: "Proposition 40 — NO — The "wealth tax" starts with billionaires but is written to allow the Legislature to raid the assets of the middle class"

subject.title: California — Proposition 41 (Prohibits New State Taxes That Exclude Revenues from State Spending Limit. Requires Audits for New State Special Taxes)

positions.statement: Transcribed from the voter guide image: "Proposition 41 — YES — Low-performing state programs should not be funded at the expense of higher-performing programs."

subject.title: California — Proposition 42 (Prohibits New State Personal Property Taxes and Certain Retroactive State Taxes)

positions.statement: Transcribed from the voter guide image: "Proposition 42 — YES — Stop the politicians from retroactively taxing your savings, investments and retirement accounts!"

subject.title: California — Proposition 43 (Limits Voters' Ability to Raise Revenues for Local Government Services)

positions.statement: Transcribed from the voter guide image: "Proposition 43 — YES — It should be more difficult, not easier, for the politicians to raise property taxes."

subject.title: California — Proposition 44 (Requires Community Health Clinics Spend 90% Of Revenue on Program Services)

positions.statement: Transcribed from the voter guide image: "Proposition 44 — NO — The politicians should not control the budgets of healthcare clinics."

subject.title: California — Proposition 45 (Modifies Environmental Review for Certain Projects)

positions.statement: Transcribed from the voter guide image: "Proposition 45 — YES — Let's reduce the amount of red tape and make it easier for government infrastructure projects to be completed."

subject.title: Irvine — Measure D (Measure Directing the Use of Ranked Choice Voting for City Council Member and Mayoral Elections after January 1, 2028)

positions.statement: Transcribed from the voter guide image: "Irvine Measure D — NO — Ranked choice voting adds unnecessary complexity to the ballot and will make local elections even more confusing than they already are."
